title: Calibrated Power of Test-Then-Pool Rules for Ternary Outcomes with Historical Controls
banked_reason: D0.5 graded incremental below the field floor; the global certificate remains open and the fixed-witness numerical certificate is not reproducible.
gap_reasons: The stated project deliverable is a width-1e-5 constrained global power certificate, but the core leaves precisely that exclusion/optimization result open and proves only a feasible-witness lower bound plus the trivial upper bound; the current kernel therefore substitutes a weaker result for the promised frontier object.

The Gaussian-tail reduction is correct, but the asserted outward quadrature bounds (7)--(8) cannot be reproduced from the node: it supplies neither the rational box partition nor the derivative/interval enclosures whose summed error is claimed, so the strict witness inequalities and every downstream gain conclusion are not discharged.

The framing correctly reserves global optimality for oeq:global-certificate, but that reservation leaves the main practical design-selection question unresolved and limits the completed paper to a specialized methodological note.
proof_attempt_summary: The run attempted a uniform local operating law, same-sample calibration, a strict fixed-design power witness, and a width-1e-5 global constrained optimum. The D0.5 review graded the delivered package incremental below the field floor because the global certificate remained open. The fixed-witness and dependent gain claims also lack reproducible interval artifacts; a retry needs an executable witness verifier and a complete global exclusion certificate.
tldr: For three independent equal-sized ternary samples, jointly calibrating selection, historical mismatch, covariance estimation, and the current-only benchmark yields a uniform local operating law for a transparent test-then-pool rule, makes its same-sample estimated-covariance calibration total with the uniform endpoint \(s=2\), outward-certifies a feasible power-improving witness, and proves a strict open-region gain over the baseline-adaptive level-\(\alpha\) Pearson test while controlling size. A width-\(10^{-5}\) certificate of the globally maximal reference power remains exclusively the open question \(\mathrm{oeq{:}global\mbox{-}certificate}\).
gap: Published test-then-pool calculations are scalar or use a different equivalence-screen and resampling procedure. None gives a total estimated-covariance calibration and a certified three-parameter optimum of the ternary raw-radius rule against a continuum of historical drifts, with power compared to a baseline-adaptive current-only test on the same neighborhood.
fill: The project supplies the joint Gaussian reduction, named random plug-in operating functionals with uniform convergence, an explicit uniform feasibility endpoint for the cutoff map, uniform level for the adaptive Pearson comparator, an outward-certified strict-gain witness, a relatively open gain region that also allows small directional historical drift, and a global interval certificate of width at most \(10^{-5}\) for the constrained power frontier.
